sections.title: Entanglement swapping across a five-node relay in a multiplexed quantum-classical network
sections.abstract: The authors report entanglement swapping across a five-node relay connected by four 10-km fibers while carrying 10-Gbps classical data on the same fibers.
sections.claimed_result: Entanglement swapping was demonstrated over 40 km total fiber length while simultaneously transmitting 10-Gbps classical data.
sections.caveat: This is not yet a deployed repeater network or fault-tolerant quantum communication system.

sections.title: A Binary Flux Calibrator Reveals the Scientific Potential of Short-integration JWST MIRI Imaging to Directly Detect sub-Jupiter Exoplanets
sections.abstract: Short, noncoronagraphic JWST MIRI exposures detected a companion to HD 101452 and imply that 17–42-second observations could detect some sub-Jupiter planets at Solar-System-like separations.
sections.claimed_result: A companion was detected in four MIRI filters; measured contrast curves suggest short integrations may reach sub-Jupiter masses for some nearby bright stars.
sections.caveat: The sub-Jupiter sensitivity is a forecast, not a direct detection of a sub-Jupiter planet.

sections.title: Kilojoule-scale laser acceleration enabling efficient generation of electron-positron and muon beams
sections.abstract: Quasi-3D PIC and Geant4 simulations propose a kilojoule-class direct-laser-acceleration regime producing high-charge pair beams and up to 6.5×10^5 Bethe–Heitler muons per shot.
sections.claimed_result: The authors estimate up to 3×10^12 positrons and 6.5×10^5 muons per shot and report simulated current-filamentation growth.
sections.caveat: Target performance, beam transport, and instability observation require experimental validation.

sections.title: Massive Galaxy Halos Contain Less Inner Dark Matter Than Predicted
sections.abstract: Combining MaNGA, ALFALFA, and SDSS group measurements, the authors find lower inner dark-matter content in massive galaxies than predicted by IllustrisTNG and EAGLE.
sections.claimed_result: Massive observed halos have lower inner dark-matter masses and central dark-matter fractions, with lower effective concentrations than predicted.
sections.caveat: The baryonic-heating explanation is plausible but model-dependent, and H I alone does not reliably determine total halo mass.

sections.title: On the importance of cosmic-ray background in the Atomki anomaly
sections.abstract: Geant4 simulations show that cosmic-muon coincidences can generate opening-angle peaks resembling features previously associated with a possible 17 MeV boson.
sections.claimed_result: Simulated cosmic backgrounds reproduce peaks near 140° and 120° in selected energy windows and can exceed internal pair conversion in the signal window.
sections.caveat: The work does not settle the origin of the Atomki excesses and calls for beam-off characterization.

sections.title: Asymmetric Inelastic Dark Matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN event
sections.abstract: The authors propose an asymmetric singlet–doublet dark-matter model that can accommodate a candidate near 250 keV in LUX-ZEPLIN while suppressing solar-annihilation constraints from IceCube.
sections.claimed_result: The model can fit the event for masses of a few hundred GeV to 1 TeV, splittings of a few hundred keV, and mixing below O(10^-2).
sections.caveat: The LZ event is an intriguing candidate, not a confirmed dark-matter detection; the interpretation is model-dependent.
